title: IGLOSS: Image Generation for Lidar Open-vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
claim: Prior pipelines rely on 2D segmenters or CLIP text-image matching; ours generates prototype images from text and matches features in a shared visual space.
layout: 3 stacked rows, each with training left and inference right; color-coded row backgrounds
description: The figure has three horizontal bands with tinted backgrounds. Pink is closed-set 3D OVSS, yellow is typical 3D OVSS with CLIP, and green is IGLOSS (ours). Columns are labeled I. Training and II. Inference. Each band is a box-and-arrow diagram with small thumbnails of camera images and lidar scans, colored module boxes, and loss or fusion symbols. Orange boxes are 2D models (2D OVSS, mask generator, CLIP, 2D VFM), blue or red boxes are 3D networks, and a green box (IG) generates template images of a car and a bus from text prompts. Lock and flame icons mark frozen and trained modules. In the IGLOSS row, text prompts go through the image generator and a 2D VFM, then are matched with 3D VFM features to produce 3D labels. A legend sits at the bottom.
caption: Examples of segment retrieval for arbitrary classes. As IGLOSS is OV, it can segment any class defined by a free text prompt. We present (points reprojected onto images) OV results for usually-ignored classes wheelchair, stroller, and crosswalk, which are not included in the 16 official nuScenes classes [ref]. Crosswalks are not even identified in nuScenes and are just labeled as any driveable surface. Although crosswalk points are geometrically on the road plane, their features identifies them specifically because the 2D-3D distillation takes lidar intensity into account [ref].
abstract: This paper presents a new method for the zero-shot open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) of 3D automotive lidar data. To circumvent the recognized image-text modality gap that is intrinsic to approaches based on Vision Language Models (VLMs) such as CLIP, our method relies instead on image generation from text, to create prototype images. Given a 3D network distilled from a 2D Vision Foundation Model (VFM), we then label a point cloud by matching 3D point features with 2D image features of these prototypes. Our method is state-of-the-art for OVSS on nuScenes and SemanticKITTI. Code, pre-trained models and generated images are available at https://github.com/valeoai/IGLOSS.
